newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak ruled partially liable in 1993 crash.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak ruled partially liable in 1993 crash.

text.p: A federal jury in Orlando ruled Friday that three companies are responsible for a 1993 Amtrak crash in Sebring, Florida, that left 59 people injured.
Friday's property damage allocation was part of an ongoing multi-party trial, Amtrak spokesman Clifford Black said. Damages for the injured passengers will be determined.

The accident occurred at a highway crossing near Intercession City, Florida, in December 1993 when a truck carrying a multi-ton electrical generator got stuck on the track causing an Amtrak Silver Meteor train to derail.
The transportation companies failed to get permission for the generator transfer from CSX Transportation, the company that owns the railroad track, Black said.
Roundtree, a trucking company, was ruled 59 percent liable for property damages while CSX Transportation was ruled 33 percent liable, and Amtrak was ruled 8 percent liable, Black said.
"We are at a loss as to why Amtrak is considered to carry any of the liability since Amtrak was a victim in this case," Black said. "And there was no indication that Amtrak had done anything wrong."
